title: AI-Generated Video Baselessly Accuses VP Candidate Tim Walz of Assault
description: WIRED found that a Russian-aligned propaganda network notorious for creating deepfake whistleblower videos was behind a coordinated effort to promote baseless claims that Minnesota governor Tim Walz sexually assaulted one of his former students. In a viral video created by generative AI and pushed by this network, someone falsely claimed to be Walz’s former student that was assaulted.

title: Fake Video Alleges Kamala Harris Involved in Hit-and-Run
description: A fake website posing as a local San Francisco news station posted a video of a woman in a wheelchair claiming that in 2011, Kamala Harris permanently injured her in a hit-and-run accident. The video was likely fabricated with generative AI, and US intelligence agencies later said that the site was created by Russia. The video was shared across Facebook, X, Reddit, TikTok, and YouTube. It received more than 10,000 views on X.

Swifties for Harris have organized to register voters, and the account for the group garnered 80,000 followers on TikTok in under a week. Swift has since endorsed Harris, citing these AI images as a driving factor for needing to make her politics known.

title: Deepfake Video of Trump Dancing with Musk Goes Viral
description: A deepfaked video appearing to show former president Donald Trump and billionaire Elon Musk dancing to the Bee Gee’s song “Stayin’ Alive” went viral on social media after Musk interviewed Trump on X. Musk has been a vocal Trump supporter, creating a pro-Trump political action committee to support his candidacy. The video was shared on TikTok and X, where Republican senator Mike Lee from Utah shared it, and it was viewed more than 3 million times.

title: Russian Influence Network Promotes Faked Obama Audio After Trump Assassination Attempt
description: In early August, a pro-Russia network of websites shared articles including deepfaked audio of former president Barack Obama. In it, Obama appears to say, “It was their only opportunity and these idiots missed it,” with regards to the Trump assassination attempt. 171 fake local news websites cited the faked audio as real, in what appeared to be AI-generated articles They were shared on X, Telegram, Facebook, and LinkedIn, among others.

title: X's Grok Spreads Election Misinformation About Kamala Harris' Eligibility
description: After President Joe Biden dropped out of the election, social media posts began to circulate showing X’s AI search assistant Grok falsely claiming that Vice President Kamala Harris had missed the deadline to appear on the ballot in nine states. In response, the secretaries of state for five of those states—Pennsylvania, Minnesota, Washington, Michigan, and New Mexico—sent a letter to X asking the company to address the problem.

title: Michigan GOP candidate releases deepfake of MLK
description: Anthony Hudson, a GOP congressional candidate running for Congress in Michigan’s 8th District, released a deepfake that appeared to show Martin Luther King Jr. endorsing him. In the deepfake, King appears to say he had another dream in which Hudson was elected to Congress.

title: AI candidate runs for mayor in Wyoming
description: Local library employee Victor Miller registered to run for mayor of Cheyenne, Wyoming, and created the Virtual Integrated Citizen (VIC), a ChatGPT-based chatbot that, he promises, will direct all of his decisions. Miller, who trained the bot on documents from past city council meetings, says he will be the chatbot’s “meat puppet,” attending meetings and doing the physical job of mayor.

title: Meta’s Llama 3 returns inaccurate information about Project 2025
description: Llama 3, Meta’s open source LLM that powers the AI functions on Instagram and Facebook, routinely returned answers effectively promoting Project 2025, according to researchers from the Global Project Against Hate and Extremism. Project 2025 is a transition plan overseen by the Heritage Foundation should a Republican win office in the 2024 presidential elections. The policy priorities include rolling back LGBTQ+ and reproductive rights, among others.

title: The Democratic National Committee makes AI parody of Lara Trump’s song
description: In response to Republican National Committee cochair Lara Trump’s song “Anything Is Possible,” the DNC released an AI-generated parody song titled “Party’s Fallin’ Down.” The song was released on Soundcloud and was promoted on X.

title: Arizona newsletter makes a deepfake of Republican senate candidate Kari Lake
description: In order to advertise its newsletter—and warn of the potential dangers of generative AI—the Arizona Agenda created a deepfake of Republican Senate candidate and 2020 election denier Kari Lake.

title: Little known US presidential candidate uses AI to campaign in American Samoa

Conversica, which worked with the campaign to build its AI-generated email and SMS campaigns, claims they reached some 44,000 prospective voters.

title: Super PAC for (former) presidential hopeful Dean Philips launches AI chatbot
description: A political action committee (PAC) supporting Congressman Dean Philips launched an AI chatbot in his brief quest as a candidate to unseat President Biden. Dean.Bot, which was built on OpenAI’s ChatGPT, could replicate the candidate’s voice to answer questions. The chatbot was shut down by OpenAI shortly after it launched for violating the company’s terms of service.

title: Democratic candidate for Congress uses AI in political ad
description: Peter Dixon, a Congressional candidate for California’s 16th District, uses AI in a campaign ad to hop between different scenes, including his home in California and an international military posting in Iraq. The video has been viewed more than 100,000 times.

title: Democratic candidates experiment with AI campaign caller Ashley
description: An AI bot called Ashley, created by the London-based company Civox, can make thousands of campaign calls in the United States and respond to each caller individually. The bot was first reported to be used by Democratic Congressional candidate Shamaine Daniels of Pennsylvania in December 2023. In February 2024, the Federal Communications Commission made it illegal to use AI-generated voices in robocalls.
